title: Textbooks Say Hair Is Pushed Out. New Imaging Says It's Pulled Up.
hook: The standard model of hair growth has cells at the follicle's base dividing and pushing the shaft upward, conveyor-belt style. Live 3D imaging reveals a hidden cellular 'motor' pulling it instead.
key_points: The textbook model held that hair grows by cell division at the follicle's base pushing the shaft upward, like a conveyor belt.
New 3D live imaging of human hair follicles in lab culture instead shows hair being actively pulled upward by surrounding tissue.
The 'motor' is the outer root sheath, whose cells move in a coordinated spiral pattern that generates mechanical pulling force.
The protein actin is essential to this process — disrupting it cut hair growth by more than 80%, showing that coordinated cell movement, not just division, drives growth.
content_html: The standard explanation for hair growth sounds simple: cells at the base of the follicle divide, and the growing hair shaft gets pushed upward, conveyor-belt style. A new study using advanced 3D live imaging suggests that's not quite right.
extra_html: Watching individual cells move in real time inside cultured human hair follicles — something ordinary microscopy can't capture — researchers found hair is actively pulled upward by the tissue surrounding it, rather than simply pushed from below. The driving force comes from the outer root sheath, whose cells move in a coordinated, spiraling pattern that mechanically tugs the shaft upward as it grows. The protein actin, which powers cell movement, turned out to be essential to the whole process: disrupting it cut hair growth by more than 80%, confirming that this coordinated pulling — not just cell division at the root — is a core part of how hair actually grows.

related.hook: Right now, millions of your cells are copying their DNA and splitting in two — the everyday process that lets you grow, heal, and replace worn-out cells.

related.title: Skin: The Body's Barrier
related.hook: Spread out, your skin would cover about two square metres — the largest organ you have, and the only one you wear on the outside.

flashcards.prompt: What did textbooks traditionally say drives hair growth, and what does this study find instead?
flashcards.back_html: Textbooks described cells at the follicle's base dividing and pushing the hair shaft upward. This study finds surrounding tissue actively pulls it upward instead, like a hidden cellular motor.

flashcards.prompt: What tissue acts as the 'motor' pulling hair upward, and how?

choices.text: The outer root sheath, whose cells move in a coordinated spiral pattern that generates pulling force
The hair shaft itself, which contracts like a muscle
Blood vessels beneath the follicle, which physically lift the hair

flashcards.explanation_html: 3D live imaging revealed the outer root sheath's cells moving in a coordinated downward spiral, and that motion generates the mechanical force pulling the hair shaft upward.

flashcards.prompt: How did researchers confirm that coordinated cell movement, not just division, drives hair growth?

choices.text: Disrupting the protein actin, essential for cell movement, cut hair growth by more than 80%
Removing the hair shaft entirely stopped follicle activity
Blocking cell division had no effect on growth at all

flashcards.explanation_html: Actin drives the mechanical force behind cell movement. When researchers disrupted it, hair growth dropped by over 80%, showing movement and force generation are essential, not just incidental to division.
